O.content: The red square has the printed inscription "37" nearby and is higher on the page than the blue circle, which has the printed inscription "143" nearby.
The blue circle has the printed inscription "139" nearby and is higher on the page than the red square, which has the printed inscription "32" nearby.
Neither the red square nor the blue circle has a visible printed numeric inscription nearby.

B.text: If the printed numbers beside the colored marks are their countries' indicator values, then the 2011 and 2013 annotations show that screen height does not reliably rank the countries' numeric values; consequently, without a printed 2012 value or explicit shared-scale information, the 2012 comparison cannot be established from mark height alone.
B.conditions: Applies only if the nearby printed numerals are values for the respective marks; it identifies an evidence gap rather than supplying a 2012 value.

O.content: A red dashed-line square is higher on the page than a blue solid-line circle.
The inscription "Canada" is printed in red beside the plot.
The inscription "United States" is printed in blue beside the plot.

B.text: If the red dashed-square series is Canada and the blue solid-circle series is United States, and both use one shared vertical scale that increases upward, then a higher 2012 mark represents a larger 2012 indicator value.
B.conditions: Assumes the colored side labels bind to their same-colored series and that the chart uses a comparable shared y-scale; no labeled y-axis values are visible.
